conflict_topics: visibility of jewellery under new uniform rule
dialogue_quality_notes: Concise, workplace-appropriate language; natural quick negotiation.
One participant raised a fairness grievance ('You made me take my earrings off.'), which prompted constructive solution-seeking.
Resolution was explicit and applied uniformly ('that goes for everyone').
evaluation.final_reason: The team agreed on a shared interpretation of the head office rule: covered items that 'can't be seen' are acceptable. Agent A changed from instructing removal to allowing covered items ('If it's covered and can't be seen, then it's fine. That goes for everyone.'), and Agent D accepted to cover the bracelet ('I'll cover it.').
position_change_notes: Agent A (shift lead) moved from a strict reading ('that means the bracelet, too') to accepting a negotiated interpretation ('If it's covered and can't be seen, then it's fine.').
Agent D initially resisted removal ('I have to keep it.') but agreed to the accommodation ('I'll cover it.').
Agent B moved from complaint about unequal treatment to accepting the common solution (implied by 'Right').
Agent C proposed a practical solution (plaster) and remained consistent as a facilitator.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'I think that means the bracelet, too.' Agent D: 'I have to keep it. Can I just cover it?' — incompatible demands (remove vs keep) expressed.
Agent A: 'As long as it can't be seen at all.' Agent B: 'Wait. You made me take my earrings off.' — introduces fairness complaint, broadening the disagreement.

Agent A: 'A bracelet can be covered. How do you cover earrings?' Agent B: 'With my headscarf. Or a plaster. You didn't suggest anything for me, you just said take them off.' — ongoing dispute about interpretation and past unequal treatment.

Agent C: 'A plaster would work. The rule is 'not visible', right?' Agent A: 'Okay, fair enough. If it's covered and can't be seen, then it's fine. That goes for everyone.' — the group agrees on a common interpretation (covered = acceptable); this settles the substantive disagreement.
Agent B: 'Right.' Agent A: 'So we're all clear for tomorrow? Everything covered.' — confirmations after the settlement.
Agent C: 'Clear.' Agent A: 'Agent D?' — routine check for confirmation; no dispute.
Agent D: 'Yeah, clear. I'll cover it.' — explicit acceptance of the agreed accommodation.
Agent A: 'Okay, good. Then we're all set for tomorrow.' — closure statement; no remaining disagreement.

substantive_insights: Primary tension was interpretive (what 'not visible' means) rather than an absolute refusal to comply with head office.
Offering concrete covering options (plaster, headscarf, cover bracelet) enabled accommodation without violating the rule.
A perceived past unequal enforcement (B's complaint) was addressed by applying the clarification to everyone, which removed that objection.
